reviews.author: Private Eye
reviews.text: Camped here for 5 days and had a magical experience! Very clean campground with super friendly staff. Wood sold every evening 4-6p. Bathrooms are clean with hot showers! Lots of critters to keep you company (the good kind) but there are some trash pandas. Would visit again AND recommend.

reviews.author: Kevin V
reviews.text:
Took my family to Sunset Bay Campground for their first taste of the Oregon coast.
They loved it!
Used it as a base camp while we visited other places each day.
Loop A is under renovation from storm damage.
The beach and surrounding areas have changed since I was there in the '80s. Very enjoyable and relaxing.
Images are not on a particular order.
Beach and Bay, local creatures, cliff vid and images are from the trail that wanders south up the mountain from Sunset Bay. Be careful on the cliff edges, stay back. Soft ground.

reviews.author: Julie Jones
reviews.text: Souch fun to introduce my granddaughters to tide pools at the same beach I learned about them. Unfortunately the park fees are steep ($12 for out of state) and the QR code wasn't working. If we hadn't been with another person that was waiting in their vehicle, we would have received a ticket

reviews.author: Matt Vickery
reviews.text: I stopped here on a road trip on a recommendation from some friends that were local to the area. I got to see the sunset at the bay, and then got a campsite across the street. The sea lions sang me to sleep, and I had a beautiful hike the next morning. 10/10 would recommend stopping and at least checking out the surrounding area.

reviews.author: Dan Brennen
reviews.text: What an incredibly beautiful place to have here. The dunes were just amazing and peaceful and I felt like I was the only one there. What a treat!

reviews.author: Jay and Heather Kuykendall
reviews.text: Older Oregon State Park, sites a little tight in spots but quiet and beautiful. Mostly treed in, was able to get Starlink coverage, although it was somewhat obstructed. Nice short walk to the beach across the road from the campground. We had a full hook-up site with 30A service, there is no dump station here if you don't get a site with sewer.

reviews.author: Jennalenore22
reviews.text: Reservation required. This campground is just a short walk from the ocean and some beautiful hiking trails that go along the coast. The spots are relatively close together, though many have trees creating some separation. I had no cell service in this area, which was welcomed for me. The showers were free, with warm water, and had many open at all times. Very quiet at night.

reviews.author: lauramp
reviews.text: At Sunset Bay State Park, we scored a full hook-up site, which made the whole stay convenient. The sites are paved and relatively level side to side. We stayed in B5, which had limited privacy. There are hedges around most of the sites. and there were nice trees and foliage at the back of B5 and along the utilities side. It's across from the hosts and near the firewood distribution area. The bathrooms and other facilities are older, though well maintained. The hosts rotated duties and were active and friendly. The campground is smaller than most along the coast and seemed quiet even though it was full. No Verizon service at B5, but I got 4 bars by the reception area and 2 bars on the beach.

reviews.author: DFH
reviews.text:
Sunset Bay is located in a great spot. There is beach access within walking distance, it is close to other interesting State Park locations. Stayed 2 nights in late May in a tent site (we travel in a self-contained camper truck). The campground is nicely shaded and clean. Part of a loop was closed for maintenance and one of the shower buildings was closed due to a broken hot water heater. The other (older) shower building was very dated but serviceable.

There was NO cell service (AT&T or Verizon). What would draw me back to this campground is the mature privacy plantings and its location.

reviews.author: CrusinSusan
reviews.text:
Yurt G. No electrical or water at the driveway, but spigot is close as is "dishwater" disposal. Short walk to toilets.

The clear tarp "window" was torn and the clips to secure the windows to the Yurt didn't line up on two of the three windows.(the Velcro didn't line up either) I tucked the curtains (inside the lattice) on one window to keep them from blowing. I remembered I had some long zip ties and, through a hole in the screen (duct taped) I managed to zip the flapping "window" to an interior piece of lattice.

The heater worked the first night but was off in the morning. I turned it up to high and it ran all day. It stopped running during the second night and I couldn't get it to work this morning. Luckily I brought a 700 watt mini radiator and put it next to my bed. It rained buckets, but I was warm and dry. (bucket toilet - who wants to get soaked at 6 am)

If you've never Yurted - bring a quilted mattress cover (thick vinyl mattresses) and back up heaters. Throw in some "handy" stuff because you never know.

You can cook on the deck, I brought a toaster oven and a mini crock pot. Made a tasty soup/stew and baked frozen enchiladas with greens. Had an electric kettle for tea and coffee. Overall not bad. There is some mold on the interior canvas and as I said the vinyl Yurt need a refurbishment (if possible) and the canvas replacing.

The showers were clean, good hot water, and the ladies had a sink with hot water - a bonus!

The park is small and densely forested, feels very remote. (no cell or wifi) of course the walks and Sunset Bay are stunning. Will return.

We stayed here in our first experience with the Oregon State Park system. Although the online reservation system said the park was completely full, we found it to be at best 2/3 full during our time there in late September.

Site D35 is full hook ups, but heavily shaded, and gets 0 cell coverage as does most the campground once you get halfway through the A loop. Most campers walked up to the check in station which did have wifi and 4 bars of 5g Verizon.

Our only complaint was the tarp city that was set up in the campsite directly across from us with people coming and going at all odd hours of the night. Numerous other campers notified the Park Rangers and staff of the issues, but we were told Oregon has some strange laws limiting their ability to enforce park rules in this circumstance...:(

Previous reviews of the sunsets at the bay, watching the seals and sea lions at the reef, and unsuccessfully trying to spot whales were unfortunately tempered a bit with having to worry about our neighbors nightly activities.

reviews.author: vmrKen
reviews.text:
We spent two nights here on our late March trek down Highway 101 in Southern Oregon. Our campsite was close to the entrance, so there was quite a bit of traffic but no obnoxious noise. Sites are paved, but the asphalt is old, uneven and cracked in places. Still, we had no trouble getting level. Sites might be a little narrower than typical for a state park, but still quite pleasant.

There are numerous walking trails, but this early in the spring they were quite muddy. The real attractions are the beaches, which certainly isn't surprising. Picturesque coves, rugged reefs and miles of sand were at our beck and call. As a bonus, we were able to enjoy a SPECTACULAR sunset. We would certainly come back!

reviews.author: camper-777119
reviews.text:
This is actually a campground for four state parks: Sunset Bay, Cape Arago, Shore Acres and Yoakam Point. If you stay here make sure you don't miss Shore Acres!

Great campground with all the facilities you usually find at Oregon state parks: clean restrooms and showers, friendly competent staff, nice campsites with adequate space between units, nice hiking trails.

Our only complaint would be they were a little stingy with the hot water. Had to shower in water that was a bit colder than lukewarm. Everything else was perfect!

reviews.author: Nathan-Helder
reviews.text:
We loved Sunset Bay State Park and we would definitely come again. Our trailer got the campsite and full hookups were great.

The lookout points in the park were fantastic and we enjoyed hiking.

The sunset was marvellous and our children enjoyed hunting for clams and sea anemones.

reviews.author: camp-roadtripper938404
reviews.text:
Pros: Beautiful setting 12 miles west of Coos Bay.

Sites have enough privacy and elbow room.

Grounds well kept.

Verizon cell service is better than last visit. Was able to stream Netflix.

Staff very friendly.

Cons: One bath house closed for repair. The bath in loop "A" needs to be remodeled/torn down!

The remaining bath house in loop "D" is decent enough, but hot is problematic.

Would we stay here again?

Yeah, with full hook-ups.

reviews.author: Casa Tortuga
reviews.text: I stayed here the first week in December 2021 coming down the Oregon coast photographing seascapes. What a really nice spot close to Shore Acres State Park. Although the surf was not what I had hoped for it's a beautiful spot and lovely botanical garden. Definitely will come back. The park was clean and friendly.

reviews.author: Ken 3d
reviews.text: This is an older state park but pretty well maintained. Close to the ocean but the access path was flooded out. Several hosts at the ready and park rangers cruising around. The campsites are generously sized with good foliage separation. One gripe is that there is no pumpout for the electric sites. Most parks have this as you exit.

reviews.author: reganbat
reviews.text: We have stayed at dozens of state parks. This one is by far the most disappointing. It is a dark and dreary campground with extremely filthy washrooms. The showers close at 7pm (3 hours earlier than most other parks). I had a sharp knock on the door of the shower at 655 and when I said I would be right out I was told "good. I'm locking it in 5 minutes" by what appeared to be a younger park attendant. When I said they closed earlier than any park Ide ever been in he said "so we can leave earlier". The road into the park is littered with bags and bags of trash. The beach is a solid 5 min walk and probably the only redeeming feature in this area (besides chucks seafood!) also.:no cell service in this campground if you need it. Ide avoid this part of the coast or look at another state park close by...lots to choose from!

reviews.author: Ross A
reviews.text: As a former Park Host I was ashamed that Sunset Bay continued to rent out Yurt H. Yurt H had a camper urinate on the mattresses on the bunk bed. No sanitation was done and was continued to be rented and not closed. We the host were instructed to hide the smell. Oct 23- Dec 23.

reviews.author: KMilFam
reviews.text: We came for the tide pooling, as recommended by a local however, we found much better tidepools and easier tidepool access at Cape Arago. Sunset here would be amazing, however it was too foggy during our visit. This is one of the best beaches in the area if you are looking for a sheltered area with a wide beach and plenty of parking. Coming here at sunrise or just before dawn is 100% doable as the path to the beach is short and without hazards. Views were pretty, and early morning was peaceful with few visitors. Later in the day it was bustling with activity, many families with children and several dogs. Tidepools here were difficult to access due to the slippery rocks, however there were many, many anemones and sea snails. We did not see sea stars here, but there were a few hermit crabs and some tiny fish. I would recommend driving another 4 miles down to Cape Arago for better tidepooling with easier access from the beach.
